task_specification.objective: Repair the complete run lifecycle around pause, resume, and retry while delivering the required player-facing choice and arena integrity capabilities, then harden the isolated dense-profile path for host qualification.

diagnosis.root_cause: The pause action is declared with no InputMap events, so Esc is consumed by context_back and never reaches the authoritative active-run pause transition. The dense qualification contract already has an editor-only profile seam, but native-renderer qualification remains unavailable; this iteration should make the candidate-side profile deterministic and recapturable without claiming native qualification.

stop_conditions: Stop after both bounded task implementations and focused code checks are complete; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own runtime recapture, visual judgment, and formal gap closure.
Do not replace, split, hide, or surgically edit the preserved CemeteryGarden authored package or any preserved coupled assets.
If native hardware evidence remains unavailable, retain the dense issue as a host qualification limitation rather than fabricating a pass.

strategy.rationale: Apply a direct InputMap and run-state ownership repair for the active defect, while separately isolating dense qualification behind deterministic editor/tester controls and bounded telemetry. This changes the root-cause strategy from prior transform tuning and keeps ordinary play behavior authoritative.

code: Run Godot parse/static checks for all edited scripts and project.godot resource loading.
White-box verify the pause action events, authoritative pause handler, edge debounce, teardown ordering, and Retry reset coverage.
Run focused checks for upgrade card rect stability, icon/value hierarchy, current-to-new delta limits, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.
Run dense_profile self-audit and inspect deterministic seed, entity caps, sample interval, history cap, release guard, cycle receipts, timeout handling, and reset-isolation rejection.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime recaptures title -> gameplay -> Esc pause -> resume -> Result -> Retry for three restarts; Tester judges frozen simulation, clean state, focus, audio, and absence of runtime errors.

Runtime/Tester recaptures the upgrade draft at the contract viewport while traversing A-B-C-B with keyboard and gamepad-equivalent input, confirming all three complete cards remain visible and actionable.

Runtime/Tester runs the isolated dense sequence serially for three complete cycles at 1920x1080 and records frame-time/FPS/entity/churn receipts plus renderer/preflight status; formal qualification remains host-owned.

Runtime/Tester samples spawn, critical route, central landmark, and perimeter views during ordinary movement to verify collision alignment, visibility, boundary behavior, and no disappearance/occlusion drift.
visual: Capture active, paused, Result, and post-Retry HUD states at the configured native resolution, checking authored focus hierarchy and no stale values.
Capture the upgrade page in unfocused, keyboard-focused, mouse-hover, and gamepad-focused states with all three cards fully rendered.
Capture sparse world views at spawn, critical route, landmark, and perimeter/ground contact, plus representative dense-wave framing for readability and occlusion review.

done_when: The pause action has an Escape binding and the supported gamepad pause/start binding; active gameplay transitions to paused exactly once per input edge, tree simulation and combat clocks freeze, and a second Escape or Resume restores the same run.

Three consecutive Result-to-Retry cycles start clean runs with reset wave, health, XP, enemies, timers, pools, audio, pause ownership, input focus, and HUD values; no stale actors, overlays, signals, or runtime errors remain.

Upgrade choices present an authored visual hierarchy with a weapon/upgrade silhouette, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in CURRENT values, and distinct keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states without clipping or sibling displacement.

The ordinary arena has larger traversable scale, a coherent external world/external depth, a visible central building/landmark, aligned collision, no disappearance or occlusion drift, a playable boundary/perimeter, and stable traversal under ordinary movement/movement replay.
The intact CemeteryGarden authored map remains the sole visual environment; only additive authoritative anchors or lifecycle/UI bindings needed for these behaviors are changed.
tasks.instructions: Repair the existing authoritative run controller, input routing, run shell, and upgrade-draft owners rather than introducing a parallel state machine. Bind Escape to the existing pause action (plus the existing gamepad pause convention), ensure edge-debounced active/paused transitions reset input latches and pause reasons, and make Retry invoke the existing teardown before beginning a fresh run. In the same bounded run-shell pass, correct the real upgrade-draft presentation so all three cards retain their complete silhouettes, icons, truthful deltas, and focus states at the shipped viewport. Rebase only spawn/objective/boundary anchors if necessary to preserve larger traversable scale and external world depth; verify the central building landmark has collision and remains visible without disappearance or occlusion during ordinary movement replay.
tasks.title: Restore pause/retry lifecycle and readable run choices

done_when: An editor/tester-only dense profile can request, resolve, advance, and reset a deterministic 25-40 enemy workload at the 1920x1080 target viewport, exercising representative weapons, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, UI, and audio without changing ordinary player sessions.

The profile enforces bounded enemy/projectile/pickup/effect work, deterministic seeding, capped history, fixed sampling intervals, and no unbounded per-frame allocations; it records frame-time distribution, FPS, active entities, churn, and runtime-error counts.

Three complete prepare -> advance -> reset cycles produce unique cycle/setup/advance receipts with reset isolation and no growth in active entities, timers, pools, or telemetry state; incomplete, duplicate, timeout, and failed-reset phases remain explicitly rejected or pending.
The dense trigger is unavailable in release exports and disabled by default; disabling it leaves the ordinary five-wave route and preserved authored world behavior unchanged.
Candidate diagnostics expose the renderer/preflight status and sample availability needed for host native qualification without treating software-renderer measurements as a pass.
tasks.instructions: Inspect the existing dense_profile.gd, run_controller.gd, wave_director.gd, and encounter_spawner.gd seam and complete only the candidate-side deterministic qualification behavior. Keep tester_dense_prepare, tester_dense_advance, and tester_dense_reset isolated behind the existing editor/release guard, use fixed workload caps and stable seeds, sample at the contract interval, and reset all spawned actors and pooled presentation state between cycles. Preserve authoritative combat and ordinary wave pacing; add or repair receipts and self-audit fields so Runtime can distinguish renderer classification, frame execution, sample availability, cycle identity, and reset isolation. Do not claim native qualification or alter the preserved authored map to improve profiling.
